reason: Although Section 4 requires return or destruction of Confidential Information, Section 5 expressly allows the Recipient to make and keep notes relating to Confidential Information, which remain governed by the agreement until destroyed, so some Confidential Information may be retained.
The definition covers any and all information provided by the State regardless of form, format, or media, which clearly implies that information conveyed verbally can be Confidential Information.

Confidential Information is defined as confidential, proprietary and trade secret information described in a CITR and marked as such; the document neither limits it to technical information nor expressly includes non-technical information.

The agreement expressly prohibits the Receiving Party from reverse engineering objects embodying the Disclosing Party's Proprietary Information, which is the agreement's term for confidential information.

The agreement expressly lets Samples, the receiving party, copy confidential information when reasonably necessary to perform his Merger Agreement obligations. That is copying permitted in some circumstances.
Section 8 expressly permits the Receiving Party to copy Confidential Information when reasonably necessary for the Scope, so copying is allowed in some circumstances.

Confidential Information is limited to information about the Invention, which is defined as technical information (products, systems, technologies) and expressly excludes business topics, so only technical information is covered.

Although clause 3.4 bars disclosure to professional advisors, the Receiving Party may still share Confidential Information with its agents and affiliates (excluded from 'third party') and with third parties given prior written consent, so sharing with some third parties is permitted.
The agreement expressly states that Confidential Information includes information disclosed orally, which is verbally conveyed information.

The agreement bars each party from soliciting the other's employees, and employees are a subset of representatives as defined in the agreement, so the receiving party may not solicit some of the disclosing party's representatives.
The definition limits Confidential Information to technical trade secrets and other technical information, so it includes only technical information.

The document expressly states that a party compelled by law to disclose confidential information is not required to give the other party prior notice, which is the opposite of the hypothesis's notification duty.

Information counts as Confidential Information only if it is conspicuously designated as Confidential, either in writing or by written confirmation after oral disclosure. So all Confidential Information has to be expressly identified.
Section 7 expressly permits the Receiving Party to make copies of Confidential Information when necessary to evaluate a Transaction, which is a circumstance in which copying is allowed.
As written, clause 5.3.2 affirmatively says disclosure gives the Recipient a licence or other rights in the Confidential Information, which is the opposite of the hypothesis that no right is granted.
The confidentiality obligations exclude information rightfully disclosed to the Receiving Party by a third party, so the Receiving Party may acquire such information from third parties.

Clause 1 says the Providing Party's information counts as confidential only if it is expressly identified as confidential when furnished. So confidential Information must be expressly identified by the disclosing party.

The agreement expressly excludes the fact that the Parties entered into the Agreement from confidential Information, so there is no obligation to keep it secret, which is the opposite of the hypothesis.
The document requires the Recipient to return or destroy all Confidential Information upon termination, which necessarily includes returning or destroying some of it.
The document expressly states that the Contractor's obligations survive termination of the Agreement, which entails that some obligations may survive termination.
The document expressly states that Confidential Information includes information disclosed orally, which is verbally conveyed information.

The only clause that addresses whether obligations continue after the deal ends says the parties stop being bound by their confidentiality and other obligations, not that those obligations survive. The agreement has no survival clause that would keep any obligation alive.
The definition limits Confidential Information to information designated as confidential at the time of disclosure, so the disclosing party has to identify it expressly for it to count.
The definition expressly limits Confidential Information to technical information or material, which matches the hypothesis that it shall only include technical information.
Section 4 expressly preserves the Recipient's right to independently develop similar information, as long as it does so without using the Confidential Information.
The agreement defines Confidential Information as only the technical information described in a CITR, so it includes only technical information.
The agreement expressly permits the signer to make copies of covered information to the extent required for official duties, so copying is allowed in some circumstances.

The Seller Parties, who are the receiving parties here, are expressly allowed to independently develop information similar to the Confidential Information, provided they do not use the Confidential Information to do it.

The definition of Evaluation Materials (the confidential information) only covers information that is specifically identified as "confidential", so confidential information must be expressly identified.

The receiving party must destroy or return all confidential information, and the only retention clause expressly says PwC may not keep a copy, so the document rules out keeping any confidential information after return or destruction.
Section 3 expressly prohibits the Receiving Party from reverse engineering any objects that embody the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, which matches the hypothesis.
The definition of Confidential Information expressly excludes information conveyed orally, so verbally conveyed information cannot be Confidential Information.
The document expressly provides that the Receiving Party's obligations survive termination, so at least some obligations of the Agreement survive termination.

The agreement expressly contemplates that Borrower may independently develop such information without violating the Agreement; it only requires that such information still be kept confidential, which restricts disclosure, not development.
